To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phospholipids flip in the membrane to facilitate the transport of annexin A2 and A2 to the outer leaflets of the plasma membrane in cells and in artificial membranes.
phospholipids play an essential role in facilitating the transport of annexin proteins from the inner leaflets of the plasma membrane and liposomes into the outer leaflets.
phospholipids play a key role in annexin transport across membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how annexin A2 and annexin A5 translocate from the cytoplamic inner leaflet of plasma membranes to the extracellular (cell surface) outer leaflet of plasma membrane.
understanding the mechanism of annexins A5 and A2 transport across the plasma membrane and the role of TMEM16F in this process.
the molecular mechanism of annexin translocation from the inner to the outer leaflets of the plasma membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phospholipid scrambling activity of TMEM16F is essential for annexin translocations to the outer leaflets of membranes.
the phospholipid scramblases TMEM16F and TMEM16K are required for annexin A2 transport across the plasma membrane.
phospholipids are flipped by TMEM16F, which allows annexin A2 to flip from the inner to the outer leaflets of the plasma membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phospholipids are crucial for annexin translocations across membranes.
phospholipids flip to the outer leaflets of the membranes, where annexins bind and flip to the inner leaflets of the membrane, where they are released.
phospholipids flip to enable annexin transport across membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
annexins are not just phospholipid-binding proteins, they also flip phospholipids.
annexins A2, A5, and other annexins, can be transported to the plasma membrane outer leaflet by a mechanism involving TMEM16F-mediated lipid scrambling.
annexin translocation to the cell surface depends on the activity of lipid scrambling proteins such as TMEM16F.
